head: 86329c1

findings.what: Round-2's auto gap IS closed: the probe now follows the same gate QwenEngine.is_available already uses for auto + VLLM_BASE_URL.
findings.why: At round-2 head 2b6c0af the predicate was just `backend in OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BACKENDS` — so `auto` + `VLLM_BASE_URL` went to Ollama. HEAD 86329c1 adds a second clause: `backend == 'auto' and bool(os.environ.get('VLLM_BASE_URL'))`. I verified: QwenEngine.is_available (engines/qwen.py:154) short-circuits True on VLLM_BASE_URL alone (HPC deployment comment confirmed), and PipelineConfig.__post_init__ (config.py:318-320) adopts VLLM_BASE_URL into qwen_vllm_url when the default is unmodified. So a user reaches vLLM by exporting ONE env var, and the cascade-halt probe now goes there with it. #222's named scenario — HPC, --strict-local, one timeout truncating the run — is no longer reachable through the configuration that triggers it.

findings.what: All four cells of the new predicate are measured and pinned.
findings.why: Re-ran the new test file in scratch worktrees against HEAD (36 passed) and against 515c680 (2 failed, 34 passed). The 2 failures match the author's report exactly: test_auto_backend_with_vllm_base_url_is_probed_at_the_vllm_server (assertion on the URL the probe hit) and test_auto_plus_vllm_base_url_is_a_known_documented_asymmetry (assertion on _local_backend_is_openai_compatible returning False instead of True). Both are behavioural AssertionErrors on _probe_backend_idle and _local_backend_is_openai_compatible — methods that exist at 515c680 — no ImportError, no AttributeError. The four cells: auto+VLLM_BASE_URL → vllm models (380), ollama+VLLM_BASE_URL → localhost/api/tags (397, the reverse-regression guard), vllm alone → vllm models (264), auto alone → localhost/api/tags (407). Explicit backend wins in both directions because the vllm/ollama branch is checked BEFORE the auto+env clause.

findings.what: My earlier 'auto limit is defensible' ruling was wrong, and the author measuring it is the right shape of correction.
findings.why: Round 2's argument was: `auto` resolves to Ollama everywhere else in this codebase, so `make_table_reader` and the probe agree there. That holds for `make_table_reader` and `resolve_qwen_intent`. It does NOT hold for `is_available` at `engines/qwen.py:154`, which short-circuits True on `VLLM_BASE_URL` alone with the explicit comment 'vLLM path (e.g. HPC, where Ollama is forbidden on server GPUs)'. A user can reach a vLLM deployment by exporting ONE env var and never touching a flag, so the probe and `is_available` were disagreeing for the exact configuration the issue is named after. My round-2 ruling is now RETRACTED in favour of round 3. The probe_and_reader_cannot_drift invariant I accepted still holds, but only when VLLM_BASE_URL is unset — which is now stated in the rescoped test_probe_and_crop_reader_agree_on_which_server_to_ask.

findings.what: The asymmetry (auto + VLLM_BASE_URL → probe vLLM, reader Ollama) is stated plainly and pinned by a test that fails loud if closed.
findings.where: tests/test_gh222_probe_host.py:410 test_auto_plus_vllm_base_url_is_a_known_documented_asymmetry, and the PR body section 'The asymmetry this leaves, stated plainly'
findings.why: On this configuration the cascade-halt probe goes to vLLM but make_table_reader still returns OllamaTableReader — so dual-pass table crops on HPC still hit an Ollama daemon that doesn't exist. The author deliberately does NOT fix it because: (a) the cascade-halt guards the whole-page qwen-ocr CLI path which DOES serve via vLLM, (b) changing the crop reader is a behavioural change to the dual-pass lane distinct from #222's scope, (c) the consequence is honest about being a real latent bug deserving its own issue. The test asserts isinstance(reader, OllamaTableReader) and says in its comment 'if this now returns a VllmTableReader the asymmetry has been closed — good, but delete this test and the PR-body note that describes it'. Closing the gap is now a deliberate act, not an accident.

findings.what: The hostile-env hazard (VLLM_BASE_URL exported bypasses probe_ollama_idle patches) is closed, verified by running four probe-patching test files under VLLM_BASE_URL=http://gpu-node.cluster:8000/v1.
findings.where: tests/test_gh222_probe_host.py fixture recorded_urls (clears VLLM_BASE_URL) plus the two new tests test_auto_backend_with_vllm_base_url_is_probed_at_the_vllm_server and test_auto_plus_vllm_base_url_is_a_known_documented_asymmetry that patch the probe by name.
findings.why: Re-ran with VLLM_BASE_URL=http://gpu-node.cluster:8000/v1 exported: 69 passed, 2 xfailed on the four probe-patching files (test_table_repair_parity, test_pp2_agentic_fuse, test_structural_gate_b1_gh151, test_landscape_refusal_a2_gh147) and 36 passed on the new test file. If the patches were silently routing past the probe, the url-asserting tests would fail or, worse, the patches-to-probe tests would pass for the wrong reason. They did not. The recorded_urls fixture monkeypatch.delenv('VLLM_BASE_URL', raising=False) keeps the new file hermetic; the two named-patch tests use monkeypatch.setattr so they don't depend on env. The author also noted all 5 files re-run green; I verified 4 of the 5 myself (the 5th is test_gh222_probe_host.py which I also ran).

findings.what: Non-vacuity accounting for the delta is honest: 2 failed at 515c680, both behavioural, on methods that already exist there.
findings.why: I re-ran the round-3 test file against 515c680 (the round-2 head, the right base to prove the auto gap specifically): 'AssertionError: an auto-backend HPC run was probed at the wrong machine' at :380 and 'assert False is True … _local_backend_is_openai_compatible' at :431. Both are AssertionErrors on _local_backend_is_openai_compatible — a method that exists at 515c680. No ImportError, no AttributeError, no signature error. HEAD 86329c1: 36 passed. Non-vacuity is sound.

findings.what: Module-level probe_ollama_idle indirection preserved in the delta.
findings.why: The delta only changes the predicate (orchestrator.py:5180-5210) and adds the VLLM_BASE_URL clause. _probe_backend_idle still calls probe_ollama_idle via the module-level name. test_existing_module_level_patches_still_reach_the_probe still passes (verified as part of the 36-pass run). All four probe-patching files run green under hostile env. No patch-silently-effected regression.

findings.what: InvalidURL escape fix from round 2 survives the delta (untouched). _had_timeout untouched. Cardinal-rule levels honest.
findings.why: _PROBE_ERRORS = (httpx.HTTPError, httpx.InvalidURL, OSError) and the parametrised IPv6 tests are unchanged between 2b6c0af and 86329c1. _had_timeout = any('timeout' in ... ) at orchestrator.py:3223 is byte-identical. The PR body still scopes to a liveness probe on a failure path (document + CLI; page + metadata untouched by design). Round 3 does not change scope; it changes only the predicate used to pick the probe target.
